question: In your research system, the web search subagent calls an MCP search tool that sometimes times out because the search service is briefly unavailable. Most of these timeouts succeed on a second attempt, but a few persist. Currently every timeout goes straight to the coordinator, which stalls the whole research flow. How should you design error handling for the web search subagent?

options.text: Retry transient timeouts within the web search subagent, and escalate to the coordinator only unresolved failures, with partial results and a record of attempts.
options.reason: The guide says to recover locally from transient failures inside subagents. Only errors that cannot be resolved locally go to the coordinator, together with partial results and what was attempted.

options.text: Return every timeout to the coordinator immediately, so that the coordinator makes all retry decisions for the web search subagent centrally.
options.reason: This is the current design. The guide says to handle transient failures locally in the subagent and to propagate only the errors that cannot be resolved there.

options.text: Retry timeouts within the web search subagent, and when retries are exhausted, return the partial results to the coordinator marked as a complete search.
options.reason: This hides an unresolved failure from the coordinator. The guide says such errors must be propagated with partial results and what was attempted, so the coordinator can decide how to recover.

options.text: Retry timeouts within the web search subagent, and when retries are exhausted, send the coordinator a generic "search failed" status without the collected results.
options.reason: The guide says a generic error status prevents appropriate recovery decisions. Escalated errors must include partial results and what was attempted.
